---
title: About and How to Use This Guide
---

## Context

Energy practitioners need reliable climate data to understand how weather and climate conditions influence electricity systems and how these conditions may evolve over time. This guide is intended to support the use of climate information in energy sector analysis and decision-making by providing a clear entry point to relevant climate datasets and to illustrate how these data can inform electric energy-related analyses. The datasets highlighted in this guide are drawn from authoritative scientific sources and represent widely used, state-of-the-art climate information available for research and application.

## Using Climate Information in the Energy Sector

Electricity systems are closely connected to climate conditions, making climate information an important input to many analytical and operational processes. Climate variability and long-term changes can affect electricity demand, resource availability, infrastructure performance, and system reliability. Understanding these relationships helps organizations assess potential risks and consider how future climate conditions may influence electric energy systems. Climate data therefore provide an important foundation for day-to-day operations and for the evaluation of future conditions to support resilient electricity sector planning.

## How to Use This Guide

The guide is designed as a practical resource that helps users connect electricity-sector questions with appropriate climate information. The pathways below provide starting points for different needs; readers can move among them as their questions develop.

## Choose a Pathway

- **[Explore an electricity-sector activity](./sectors/electricity_sector_activities.qmd):** Begin with a planning, operational, infrastructure or reporting task and identify relevant climate inputs, methods and decisions.
- **[Understand climate data](./datasets/Climate_Datasets_Overview.ipynb):** Review foundational explanations of projections, scenarios, ensembles, downscaling, uncertainty and data formats.
- **[Find and compare climate datasets](./guidance/Climate_Data_Decision_Tree.qmd):** Select data by decision context, dataset category, variable or documented product.
- **[Apply climate data](./adaptation/Adaptation.qmd):** Explore how climate information can support adaptation, vulnerability, risk and related decision analyses.
- **[Build organizational capability](./maturity_matrix/Maturity_Matrix.qmd):** Assess organizational maturity, barriers, procurement practices and oversight capacity.
- **[Use resources, examples and tools](./guidance/Climate_Information_Ressources.qmd):** Find external climate-information portals, example applications and analysis-support tools.

## Supporting Climate-Informed Energy Decisions

By connecting climate datasets with real-world applications, the guide aims to make climate information more accessible and usable for energy practitioners. It provides a structured overview of [types of climate data](./datasets/Climate_Datasets_Overview.ipynb) and guidance on [applying climate information](./adaptation/Adaptation.qmd) in analysis and decision workflows. In doing so, the guide supports consistent and informed consideration of climate conditions in [electricity-sector planning, operations and management](./sectors/electricity_sector_activities.qmd). The guide also includes a [Maturity Matrix](./maturity_matrix/Maturity_Matrix.qmd) for self-assessment that helps organizations reflect on how climate information is currently incorporated into their processes and identify opportunities to strengthen climate-informed practices over time.
